newsitem.title: USA: Garvey confirmed by Senate to head FAA.
newsitem.headline: Garvey confirmed by Senate to head FAA.

text.p: The Senate late Thursday confirmed Jane Garvey as administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration.

An FAA spokesman said Friday that Garvey would probably be sworn in next week. A former director of Boston's Logan International Airport, she was most recently the acting head of the Federal Highway Administration.
Garvey will be the first FAA administrator appointed to a five-year term. She will also steer the FAA under a new mandate that makes clear that air safety is the FAA's top priority.

Previous FAA administrators served at the pleasure of the president. Garvey's predecessor, David Hinson, who had said he would not serve beyond President Clinton's first term, left the FAA last November after three years in the job.
"I will use the tools Congress has given the FAA to assure the American people that safety is the highest priority of the FAA," Garvey said in a statement.
